title: Janus Infinite Faces — Multi-Root Independence and Trust-Sybil Test
test_question: If one external root may fail, can Janus safely rely on several roots without mistaking many keys controlled by one authority for independent witnesses?

failed_design.attack: One authority creates ROOT_A1, ROOT_A2 and ROOT_A3 under the same administrative and infrastructure control, then satisfies its own threshold.

cases.name: two independent domains bind same state/verifier/policy coordinate
three domains disagree 1/1/1
cases.note: Do not average incompatible state roots.

quorum_rule.name: DOMAIN_DIVERSE_ATTESTATION_QUORUM
requirements: record dissent rather than delete it
quorum_rule.limitation: Two compromised independent domains can still collude; quorum reduces a failure class but does not create absolute truth.

identity_parallel.face_sybil: Many faces do not create many votes.
identity_parallel.trust_sybil: Many keys in one failure domain do not create many independent witnesses.

next_gate.name: JANUS_INFINITE_FACES_POST_COMPROMISE_TEMPORAL_ROOT_RECOVERY_TEST
next_gate.question: What happens when a root that legitimately attested old checkpoints becomes compromised later?
